hints: Set up the equation of motion for particle A ($2\text{ kg}$) descending vertically and particle B ($3\text{ kg}$) ascending the $18^\circ$ smooth slope: $2g - 3g\sin 18^\circ = (2 + 3)a$.
Find the common acceleration $a_1$ and calculate the speed squared $v^2$ when A hits the ground ($s_1 = 0.45\text{ m}$) using $v^2 = 2a_1(0.45)$.
After A hits the ground, the string breaks and B moves freely up the smooth incline under gravity alone: deceleration is $a_2 = -g\sin 18^\circ$.
Find the additional distance $s_2$ using $0 = v^2 + 2a_2 s_2$, then add $s_1 + s_2$ to find the total distance.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the connected system before A hits the ground ($m_A = 2\text{ kg}$, $m_B = 3\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$2g - 3g\sin 18^\circ = (2 + 3)a$$
$$20 - 30\sin 18^\circ = 5a$$
$$20 - 9.27051 = 10.72949 = 5a \implies a = 2.1459\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find the speed $v$ when A reaches the ground after descending $s_1 = 0.45\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(2.1459)(0.45) = 1.9313\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$$

After the string breaks, B moves up the smooth $18^\circ$ incline under its weight component alone:
$$-3g\sin 18^\circ = 3a_2 \implies a_2 = -g\sin 18^\circ = -10\sin 18^\circ \approx -3.0902\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find the further distance $s_2$ travelled by B before coming to instantaneous rest:
$$0 = v^2 + 2a_2 s_2$$
$$0 = 1.9313 - 2(3.0902)s_2$$
$$6.1804 s_2 = 1.9313 \implies s_2 = \frac{1.9313}{6.1804} \approx 0.3125\text{ m}$$

Calculate the total distance travelled by B:
$$s_{\text{total}} = s_1 + s_2 = 0.45 + 0.3125 = 0.762\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Finds coupled acceleration $a = 2.146\text{ m s}^{-2}$, evaluates $v^2 = 1.931\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$, finds free-flight deceleration $a_2 = -3.090\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to get extra distance $0.312\text{ m}$, yielding total distance $0.762\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Divide the motion of particle $B$ into two stages:
- Stage 1: Both particles $A$ and $B$ are connected by the taut string until $A$ hits the ground ($s_1 = 0.45\text{ m}$).
- Stage 2: The string breaks, and particle $B$ continues to slide freely up the smooth $18^\circ$ inclined plane until coming to instantaneous rest.

Analyse Stage 1:
Write Newton's second law for each particle:
- For particle $A$ ($2\text{ kg}$) moving vertically downwards:
$$m_A g - T = m_A a \implies 2g - T = 2a$$
- For particle $B$ ($3\text{ kg}$) moving up the $18^\circ$ incline:
$$T - m_B g\sin 18^\circ = m_B a \implies T - 3g\sin 18^\circ = 3a$$
Add the two equations to eliminate tension $T$:
$$2g - 3g\sin 18^\circ = (2 + 3)a$$
Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$20 - 30\sin 18^\circ = 5a$$
Compute $30\sin 18^\circ$ using $\sin 18^\circ \approx 0.309017$:
$$30(0.309017) \approx 9.27051\text{ N}$$
$$20 - 9.27051 = 10.72949 = 5a$$
$$a = \frac{10.72949}{5} \approx 2.14590\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the speed squared $v^2$ when particle $A$ hits the ground over distance $s_1 = 0.45\text{ m}$ from rest ($u = 0$):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2a s_1 = 0 + 2(2.14590)(0.45) = 0.9(2.14590) \approx 1.93131\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$$

Analyse Stage 2 after the string breaks:
Particle $B$ now moves up the smooth inclined plane with no tension ($T = 0$). The only force parallel to the plane is the component of gravity down the incline:
$$\sum F_\parallel = m_B a_2$$
$$-m_B g\sin 18^\circ = m_B a_2$$
$$a_2 = -g\sin 18^\circ = -10\sin 18^\circ \approx -3.09017\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the further distance $s_2$ travelled by $B$ up the slope until coming to rest ($v_{\text{final}} = 0$):
$$0^2 = v^2 + 2a_2 s_2$$
$$0 = 1.93131 + 2(-3.09017)s_2$$
$$6.18034 s_2 = 1.93131$$
Divide by $6.18034$:
$$s_2 = \frac{1.93131}{6.18034} \approx 0.31249\text{ m}$$

Sum the distances from both stages to find the total distance travelled by particle $B$:
$$s_{\text{total}} = s_1 + s_2 = 0.45 + 0.31249 \approx 0.76249\text{ m}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$s_{\text{total}} = 0.762\text{ m}$$
Thus the total distance travelled by $B$ before coming to instantaneous rest is $0.762\text{ m}$.
